observed_text: Sharp branches ω(q) are measured in crystals; the wavevector is defined against the lattice (2π/a = 1.16e10 m⁻¹ for Si with a = 5.431 Å, 1.76e10 m⁻¹ for diamond with a = 3.567 Å). A crystal of N atoms has exactly 3N modes.
implied_text: The hardware is the crystalline lattice. The map as a spectrum is an extended-crystal object with no single length attached.
description: Phonon dispersion requires an ordered grid; one cell is the repeating unit and the spectrum is many-cell. Amorphization loses the sharp branches.
value_text: primitive cell + extended crystal; no single length
notes: Lattice constants from the Ioffe archive: Si 5.431 Å; diamond 3.567 Å. The aluminium value was dropped (not opened).

observed_text: The highest listed phonon frequency is the zone-centre optical mode: 15.5 THz in Si (300 K) and 39.9 THz in diamond. Zone-boundary modes lie at 3.45–14.7 THz in Si and 16.9–37.6 THz in diamond. Acoustic branches run from zero with slope equal to the sound speed (Si [100] 8.43 km/s).
implied_text: ω_s(q) is the allowed-clock table. Nothing in the lattice oscillates as a phonon faster than the highest measured branch.
description: The lattice’s mechanical clocks are the measured branches, from acoustic zero up to a material-typical THz ceiling.
value_text: 0 to 15.5 THz (Si); 0 to 39.9 THz (diamond)
notes: value_si is the Si zone-centre optical frequency. The earlier Al ~10 THz ceiling was dropped: no opened source.

observed_text: A mode holds energy ħω(n+½). At a displacive transition a branch frequency falls toward zero, which is loss of the restoring constraint along one coordinate.
implied_text: This is an oscillator budget, not an activation barrier that holds a directional state. Dispersion is not a latch.
description: Phonon branches are driven oscillators, not a memory. There is no static barrier holding a written mechanical state.
value_text: ħω(n+½) oscillator budget, not KV
notes: Negative latch spec: contrast with permanent-magnet-latch.

observed_text: No lattice mode exists above the highest branch: 15.5 THz in Si, 39.9 THz in diamond. The Debye frequency kΘ_D/h (13.3 THz for Si at 640 K, 38.8 THz for diamond at 1860 K) lies below that measured top. q outside the first zone is an alias.
implied_text: Drive faster than the last branch finds no lattice mode. The edge is the measured maximum of ω(q), not the Debye frequency.
description: The allowed-clock table ends at the zone-boundary maximum; faster drive is not a phonon.
value_text: ω above last branch (Si 15.5 THz; diamond 39.9 THz)
notes: Debye ω_D is the fitted stand-in filed under debye-cutoff; it is not the ceiling of the real spectrum.

observed_text: In displacive structural transitions (PbTiO3, BaTiO3, SrTiO3, quartz) a branch frequency falls toward zero as the transition is approached. Order–disorder systems such as NaNO2 show no soft mode above 1e11 Hz. Melting is not preceded by one: the crystal keeps a finite shear modulus up to its melting point.
implied_text: Softening to ω→0 closes one restoring channel and a displacive structural change follows. It is not a precursor of melting.
description: A branch that loses its restoring frequency is a coordinate-specific instability at a displacive transition, continuous in temperature.
value_text: ω → 0 (soft mode)
notes: Limited to displacive transitions. The predicted row soft-mode-before-tm is contradicted for ordinary melting.

observed_text: Melting is first-order and ends the crystal that carries the branches, with no softening first (finite shear modulus up to the melting point). Finite lifetime broadens a peak without removing the branch.
implied_text: The clock table is carried by the crystal. Destroy the crystal and the map of sharp branches ends.
description: Melting or amorphization removes the allowed-clock table by destroying the lattice that defined q.
value_text: melting / amorphization; sharp branches gone
notes: The melting threshold itself is owned by melting.

observed_text: Acoustic slopes equal measured sound speeds (Al longitudinal 6374 m/s, shear 3111 m/s; Si [100] 8.43 and 5.84 km/s; diamond [100] 17.52 and 12.82 km/s). Zone-centre optical frequencies: Si 15.5 THz (517 cm⁻¹), diamond 39.9 THz (1331 cm⁻¹).
implied_text: The stable output is the measured surface ω_s(q), its long-wave speeds v_s, and its zone-centre optical frequencies, for as long as the crystal remains ordered.
description: The synchronized ion grid emits a material-typical allowed-clock map, not a single binary macro.
value_text: ω_s(q); v_s; Γ optical modes (Si 15.5 THz; diamond 39.9 THz)
notes: Long-wave slope is also speed-of-sound. No single dispersion threshold is attached.

observed_text: QSA takes the measured ω(q) as data. Force-constant models that fit the curves are not promoted to node rules. The mapping does not predict which crystal will soften.
implied_text: Branch frequencies are located as the clock table but not derived from a more primitive set of node spring constants.
description: The allowed-clock map is taken, not computed from node springs. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
value_text: ω(q) taken, not derived
notes: File-level mapping is Medium: hardware scale is not a single number; binary macros belong to related lattice entries.

observed_text: The continuum speed holds for wavelengths long against the node spacing. A vacuum has no medium. Liquids are tabulated with one compressional speed; solids with a longitudinal and a shear speed.
implied_text: Hardware is a coupled mechanical population with many nodes per wavelength, plus the relevant restoring modulus.
description: Sound requires a medium and the modulus that provisions the claimed branch. Vacuum has no nodes; fluids do not provision shear.
value_text: λ ≫ a; medium + modulus

observed_text: Dry air at 0 °C: 331.46 ± 0.10 m s⁻¹; at 20 °C and 10 % humidity 343.5 m s⁻¹. Distilled water at 20 °C: 1482.36 m s⁻¹. Mild steel: 5960 m s⁻¹ bulk longitudinal, 5196 rod, 3235 shear. Copper 4759 and 2325; aluminium 6374 and 3111 m s⁻¹.
implied_text: The long-wave clock speed is the q→0 slope of the acoustic branch on the same grid phonon-dispersion maps at finite q. No single v_s is universal.
description: Sound speed is the material-typical √(C/ρ) slope, not a universal constant.
value_text: air 343.5 m/s (20 °C); water 1482 m/s; mild steel 5960 / 3235 m/s
notes: value_si left null: examples, not one pin. Speeds computed from K, G and density agree with the measured ones within 0.3 % for Cu, Al, Ni. Polyatomic gases disperse near a relaxation frequency (CO₂ 280 → 293 m/s).

observed_text: Transit time on a path L is t = L/v_s. Computed: 5 m of air 14.6 ms; 5 m of steel rod 0.96 ms; 5 cm of steel rod 9.6 µs.
implied_text: The macroscopic acoustic clock is the transit L/v_s and the period λ/v_s, not the Debye ceiling.
description: A laboratory path is about 15 ms in air and about 1 ms in steel over 5 m; microseconds apply to centimetres of metal.
value_text: t = L/v_s; 14.6 ms (5 m air); 0.96 ms (5 m steel rod)
notes: Corrected: the first version gave microseconds for a metal bar of room length.

observed_text: The operating condition is a finite restoring modulus (bulk, and shear if a shear wave is claimed) plus a density. The wave is a launched collective oscillation, not a memory.
implied_text: No latched barrier. Presence of C and ρ provisions the slope; holding a sound field is not a zero-power memory.
description: Sound is a driven collective oscillation of coupled nodes, not a stored directional state.
value_text: finite C and ρ; no latch

observed_text: A vacuum has no coupled mechanical medium: no wave is launched and v_s is undefined there.
implied_text: No nodes, no wave. Vacuum is missing hardware, not a limiting speed of zero.
description: Sound dies when the coupled medium is absent. v_s is undefined in vacuum.
value_text: vacuum: v_s undefined

observed_text: Liquids are tabulated with one compressional speed (liquid tin 2471 m s⁻¹ at 240 °C, liquid zinc 2780 at 450 °C). On melting the static shear modulus goes from a finite value to zero. Liquid gallium carries transverse excitations only above a wavevector of 9 nm⁻¹, with a lifetime of 0.5 ps and a range of 0.4–0.5 nm.
implied_text: G = 0 at acoustic frequencies means the shear restoring coupling is absent in the liquid. The compressional wave remains. At picosecond periods a liquid still responds transversely over a few atomic spacings.
description: No static shear modulus, no shear sound wave. Melting removes the solid's shear wave in a jump.
value_text: G = 0 in the liquid at acoustic frequencies; shear wave lost at T_m
notes: Cross-cite melting. The exception at THz frequency is a crossover in frequency, filed in the effect file.

observed_text: A pair {v_L, v_T} in a solid or a single speed in a fluid, fixed by modulus and density. Examples: air 343.5 m s⁻¹ at 20 °C; water 1482 m s⁻¹; mild steel 5960 and 3235 m s⁻¹; copper 4759 and 2325 m s⁻¹.
implied_text: The synchronized long-wavelength output of the coupled mechanical population is that material-typical slope set.
description: The machine emits a handbook v_s class, not one universal speed.
value_text: {v_L, v_T} solid; v_L fluid (air 343.5; water 1482; steel 5960 / 3235 m/s)
notes: Same springs as elasticity, read as a slope. qa ~ 1 moves the mode onto the phonon-dispersion curve.

observed_text: A closed mapping would say why a given solid has the C it has, from node-spring rules, rather than taking handbook moduli as input. The speed measurement does not depend on closing it.
implied_text: QSA takes measured C and ρ and reads v_s = √(C/ρ). It does not derive the moduli from node springs.
description: The slope is located; the springs that set C are not derived here. Same gap as elasticity.
value_text: C, ρ taken; v_s = √(C/ρ)
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Ideal-gas air and condensed water share the Newton–Laplace form on different hardware; ideal-gas-pressure owns the wall force, not this slope.

observed_text: N atoms give exactly 3N normal modes; the count is finite, unlike the modes of the electromagnetic field in a cavity.
implied_text: The clock ceiling exists because the node count is finite. A macroscopic crystal still has a highest mechanical frequency.
description: Finite N is the hardware: 3N modes, no more. The Debye sphere is only a way to place that count on a linear spectrum.
value_text: 3N modes (3 per atom)
notes: A molecule or cluster has a discrete vibrational set and no continuum Debye sphere.

observed_text: Debye temperatures: Pb 105 K (0 K limit) and 87 K (298 K fit); Si 640 K; diamond 1860 K. Debye frequency kΘ_D/h: 2.2 THz (Pb), 13.3 THz (Si), 38.8 THz (diamond).
implied_text: ω_D is the clock ceiling of the ion grid under the linear-spectrum count. Below it only a T³-growing fraction of the 3N modes is in play; above it the mechanical spectrum is fully occupied.
description: The Debye clock runs from 2.2 THz (Pb) to 38.8 THz (diamond), a fitted stand-in for the top of the measured spectrum.
value_text: 2.2 THz (Pb) to 38.8 THz (diamond)
notes: value_si is the Pb value. The measured top of the spectrum lies above ν_D in Si (15.5 THz) and diamond (39.9 THz).

observed_text: ħω_D = kΘ_D is defined by fitting a continuous density of states to 3N modes. It is a spectral edge of a model, not an activation energy.
implied_text: No latched barrier. Θ_D organizes occupation of the last modes; it does not hold a written state.
description: The Debye edge is a cutoff on the oscillator table, not a KV-style memory barrier.
value_text: ħω_D = kΘ_D spectral edge, not a latch
notes: Θ_D is not a melting temperature.

observed_text: Beyond the 3N-th mode there is no lattice mode. In the Debye model that edge is ω_D; in the measured crystals the top branch lies above ν_D (Si 15.5 against 13.3 THz; diamond 39.9 against 38.8 THz).
implied_text: Drive or thermal weight above the top branch finds no lattice mode to occupy. ω_D approximates that edge and is not itself the edge.
description: Above the finite-mode ceiling there is no further phonon channel. The ceiling is the measured top branch; ω_D is a fit.
value_text: ω above top branch (mode absent); ω_D approximate
notes: The heat-capacity approach to 3Nk is a crossover along the Debye function, scale Θ_D.

observed_text: Lead has C_p = 26.84 J/(mol K) at 298.15 K (1.08 × 3R) and melts at 600.612 K, 5.7 times its low-temperature Debye temperature. Diamond at room temperature is at 0.25 of 3k per atom.
implied_text: Melting removes the crystalline mode table. Exceeding Θ_D does not.
description: Grid destruction, not Θ_D overrun, ends the 3N crystalline clocks.
value_text: melting ends 3N modes; Θ_D ≠ T_m (Pb T_m = 600.612 K = 5.7 Θ_D)
notes: Cross-cite melting. The earlier remark that diamond does not melt at 1 atm was dropped (not sourced here).

observed_text: The Debye form assumes a continuous density of states holding 3N modes. A small N gives discrete lines; a single ω_D on a real crystal is a fit that moves with temperature (Pb: 105 K to 87 K).
implied_text: The continuum cutoff is a large-N object. Under-provisioned N is a different spectrum, not a lower Θ_D of the same machine.
description: A cluster does not run a Debye sphere. Continuum Θ_D requires a lattice large enough for the q_D integral.
value_text: N too small → discrete lines, not Debye
notes: No size scale filed.

observed_text: Θ_D: Pb 105 K (0 K) and 87 K (298 K); Si 640 K; diamond 1860 K. Heat capacity as a fraction of the Dulong–Petit value near room temperature: Pb 1.08, Si 0.79, diamond 0.25. Low-T insulator heat capacity follows T³; metals add γT.
implied_text: A material-typical Θ_D and the two heat-capacity limits it organizes are the averaged output of a finite, synchronized mechanical population.
description: The finite-mode machine emits a Θ_D from about 100 K (Pb) to 1860 K (diamond), with T³ and 3Nk as the organized limits.
value_text: Θ_D 87–105 K (Pb) to 1860 K (diamond)
notes: Any one Θ_D is medium: it depends on fit method and temperature. Metals add a γT term owned by electron-heat-capacity.

observed_text: Placing the ceiling at one spherical ω_D is an interpolation: the measured top branch lies above ν_D in Si and diamond. QSA takes fitted Θ_D as the clock specification and does not derive it.
implied_text: The 3N ceiling is tight; the Debye-sphere pin is taken, not derived.
description: Finite mode count is closed. A single spherical Θ_D is an interpolation over the real zone boundary.
value_text: Θ_D taken; sphere vs zone boundary
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Gap is the sphere versus the real zone boundary, not the existence of a cutoff.

observed_text: A crystal large enough for the bulk value to hold. Gold particles down to 20 Å melt lower: 2.5 nm gold at 320 K (corrected) or about 673 K (uncorrected) against 1337 K for the bulk; 4.1 nm at 782 K and 1.6 nm at 405 K by an electrochemical transition. The depression is roughly proportional to 1/d.
implied_text: The hardware is an ordered lattice large against a few nanometres. Below that the melting temperature falls roughly as the inverse diameter.
description: Bulk melting needs a crystal much larger than a few nanometres; micrometre powder is bulk for this purpose.
value_text: bulk T_m for d ≫ nm; Au 2.5 nm: 320–673 K vs 1337 K
notes: Glasses have no crystalline order to lose; that statement is not sourced in the file.

observed_text: Melting is limited by heat supply and by nucleation at a surface. Gold-coated silver spheres of about 130 µm stayed solid at least 7.5 K above the melting point of silver for about one minute; without a coating superheating is a few degrees or less.
implied_text: The conversion clock is heat supply and surface nucleation; no material clock is filed.
description: Melting starts at a surface; with the surface blocked a crystal can be held above T_m for about a minute.
value_text: nucleation-limited; ≥ 7.5 K superheat for ~1 min (coated Ag)
notes: The comparison with Debye temperatures (Pb, diamond) was dropped: no opened source.

observed_text: Melting points at one atmosphere: Zn 692.73 K, Al 933.45 K, Cu 1358 K, Ni 1728 K, Fe 1809 K; W 3660–3695 K. Enthalpy of fusion: Cu 207, Al 397, Fe 247, Ni 292, Zn 112 kJ kg⁻¹. From 300 K to fully liquid: Cu 673, Al 1062, Fe 1297, Ni 1098, Zn 277 kJ kg⁻¹ (6.03, 2.87, 10.21, 9.78, 1.97 GJ m⁻³).
implied_text: Two numbers per material: the temperature T_m and the enthalpy of fusion. Reaching T_m is not sufficient; fusion is 19–40 % of the heat needed from room temperature.
description: T_m and the enthalpy of fusion are measured gates of the lattice, not derived barriers.
notes: value_si left null: several pins. Enthalpies computed from NIST-JANAF entries; tin estimated at about 109 kJ/kg.

observed_text: At T_m for the given pressure the solid converts to liquid with a latent heat, and the static shear modulus goes from a finite value to zero. T_m rises 3.3 (Sn), 4.3 (Zn) and 7.0 (Al) K per kilobar. A surface-coated crystal has been held 7.5 K above T_m for about a minute.
implied_text: Loss of the ordered lattice at the measured coexistence temperature. The shear wave and static shear stiffness end with the solid, in a jump.
description: The lattice fails at T_m: latent heat, G from finite to zero, one sound wave left.
notes: Cross-cite speed-of-sound and elasticity. No soft-mode precursor in the sources opened.

observed_text: Order can also be lost below T_m by heavy plastic strain, irradiation or dissolution. No source was opened and no measured scale is filed.
implied_text: Those are lattice-destruction routes, not the thermal coexistence cliff.
description: Plastic strain, radiation, or dissolution can erase the grid without reaching T_m.
value_text: plastic strain / radiation amorphization / dissolution
notes: Unsourced statement kept as a named route. Latch entries may list lattice loss as a secondary failure.

observed_text: A material constant T_m(P), reproducible to about 0.1 mK in pure metals used as temperature fixed points (Sn 505.078 K, Zn 692.677 K, Al 933.473 K, Cu 1357.77 K), and a fixed enthalpy of fusion: Cu 13.14, Al 10.71, Fe 13.81, Ni 17.16, Zn 7.32 kJ mol⁻¹.
implied_text: The stable product is the coexistence temperature itself plus the solid/fluid sides of the cliff.
description: The output is a solid below T_m and a first-order conversion at a reproducible temperature with a fixed latent heat.
notes: Pressure slope 3.3–7.0 K per kbar (Sn, Zn, Al).

observed_text: Lindemann criterion: melting when the rms displacement reaches about one tenth of the interatomic distance; it is not very accurately fulfilled. Reported ratios span 0.12–0.19 (0.15–0.16 fcc, 0.18–0.19 bcc) and are not universal.
implied_text: QSA takes measured T_m as the empirical threshold. Lindemann is a displacement consistency check, not a derived barrier.
description: The mapping does not close on why a metal melts at its particular temperature. Lindemann is a rule of thumb, not a node-level derivation.
value_text: √⟨u²⟩/a ≈ 0.1–0.19 at T_m (criterion; not universal)
notes: File-level mapping is Medium while T_m data are High. Cohesive well depth, coordination, and anharmonicity (thermal-expansion) enter and are not yet primitive node specifications. Soft-mode melting belongs with phonon-dispersion. value_si is the 0.1–0.15 window midpoint.

observed_text: A lattice with propagating acoustic modes plus a mean free path: about 10⁻⁴ cm in glasses at 2 K, falling as T⁻⁴ at higher temperature; within 10 nm for phonons in metals at room temperature.
implied_text: Hardware is the phonon-carrying lattice plus the scattering length ℓ. When ℓ reaches the specimen size the specimen is the buffer.
description: Phonon κ requires a propagating lattice and an ℓ. Casimir makes the specimen the spatial buffer; a glass never provisions the crystal peak.
value_text: ℓ ~ 1 µm (glass, 2 K); < 10 nm (phonons in metals, 300 K)
notes: In metals phonons carry 1–40 % of the heat (Cu 4.7 %, Al 3.5 %, Ni 12.5 %).

observed_text: Carrier speed v is the long-wave acoustic slope. The transport clock is the scattering time τ = ℓ/v: boundary-limited and long at low T, umklapp-limited and short at high T. Zone-boundary / Debye periods remain the underlying oscillator clocks.
implied_text: Transport latency is ℓ/v, not the Debye period. No single τ is extracted.
description: The heat-current clock is the scattering time set by ℓ. Oscillator clocks stay with debye-cutoff.
value_text: τ = ℓ/v (unpinned)
notes: v owned by speed-of-sound; C(T) by debye-cutoff; this file owns ℓ. Kinetic-theory statement; no source opened for a scattering time.

observed_text: No latched barrier. Umklapp is a kinematic threshold in the phonon population (enough large-q modes occupied) rather than an activation barrier that stores a state. T → 0 starves C; T → T_m removes the grid.
implied_text: The transport spec has occupation and grid conditions, not a memory barrier.
description: Phonon heat current is not a latch. Umklapp is kinematic; T → 0 or melting starve the channel.
value_text: umklapp kinematic; C→0 as T→0; grid to T_m

observed_text: κ scales with ℓ. Natural diamond (1.07 % ¹³C) is about 2200 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at room temperature and an isotopically pure crystal about 3100. Glasses agree with one another within a factor of 5 from 0.05 to 100 K and show no crystal-like peak. In vitreous silica anharmonicity has a negligible effect on heat transport.
implied_text: ℓ is the load-bearing transport resource. Shorten it and the heat current dies even while the modes still exist.
description: The transport spec degrades as the mean free path shortens: isotopes, defects, disorder, and phonon–phonon scattering at high temperature.
value_text: ℓ set by isotopes, defects, disorder; diamond 2200 → 3100 W/m/K on isotope removal
notes: The 1/T umklapp law is a textbook statement and was not sourced.

observed_text: Specimen size below the bulk ℓ makes κ follow the smallest dimension; with C ∝ T³ this gives κ ∝ T³ at low temperature in a clean insulator. Textbook statement; no source was opened and no measured scale is filed.
implied_text: Spatial under-provisioning of the path makes the sample the buffer. That is a size failure of the bulk-κ spec.
description: When L < intrinsic ℓ, the heat current is boundary-limited and κ tracks the specimen, not bulk umklapp.
value_text: L ≲ ℓ (Casimir); κ ∝ T³ at low T
notes: Any one peak temperature or residual ℓ is sample-dependent (medium).

observed_text: The crystal's phonon population ends at T_m. In a metal the conductivity drops sharply on melting and stays large because the electronic channel continues; the lattice contribution in liquid metals is about two orders of magnitude below the electronic one (tertiary source).
implied_text: Destroy the lattice and the crystal's phonon κ is gone. In a metal the measured κ is mostly electronic on both sides of T_m.
description: Melting ends the crystal's phonon heat current. A metal's measured κ drops and does not vanish.
value_text: T_m: lattice channel ends; a metal keeps its electronic κ
notes: Cross-cite melting and electron-heat-capacity. No opened source gives an insulator's κ across T_m.

observed_text: Room temperature: natural diamond about 2200 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, isotopically pure about 3100. A 99.9 % ¹²C diamond reaches 41 000 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 104 K. Lattice part in metals: 2–18 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (Cu 17.6, Al 8.1, Ni 14.5).
implied_text: A material- and size-dependent κ(T) with the crystal peak-and-fall shape, produced by a synchronized phonon population limited by ℓ.
description: The transport machine emits a κ(T) set by heat capacity, sound speed and mean free path: thousands of W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ in diamond, 2–18 for the lattice part in metals.
value_text: diamond 2200–3100 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (300 K); lattice part in metals 2–18
notes: value_si is natural diamond at room temperature. The oxide-glass figure of about 1 W/m/K was removed: not sourced.

observed_text: The mapping takes the kinetic formula and the Peierls umklapp distinction as descriptive data. It does not yet extract a particular ℓ(T) from node-level anharmonicity.
implied_text: The failing resource (ℓ) is identified; its value is not derived from node rules.
description: QSA names ℓ as the transport buffer but does not compute ℓ(T) from anharmonicity. Same unfinished anharmonicity as thermal-expansion.
value_text: κ = (1/3) C v ℓ taken; ℓ(T) underived
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Electronic thermal conductivity belongs with the electron population.

observed_text: A coupled lattice for E and G; a fluid suffices for K. The yield stress is set by a mesoscale population of dislocations and grain boundaries and follows σ_y = σ_0 + k d^(−1/2) with grain size d (coefficients not read).
implied_text: Hookean E is a grid average. Yield is a different, defect-structure buffer on the same crystal.
description: Small-strain stiffness lives on the ion grid; plasticity lives on a mesoscale defect population.
value_text: lattice for E, G; yield ∝ d^(−1/2) (Hall–Petch)
notes: Elastomers are entropy-elastic and not this ion-grid machine.

observed_text: Elastic strain at yield, A/E: OFHC copper 6.9×10⁻⁴, Nickel 200 8.2×10⁻⁴, Armco iron 8.3×10⁻⁴, 1006 steel 1.65×10⁻³, 4340 steel 3.7×10⁻³, 2024 aluminium 3.8×10⁻³.
implied_text: The linear restoring output is specified only inside that small-strain window.
description: The metals tabulated stay linear only to strains of 0.07–0.4 %.
value_text: strain ≤ 0.07–0.4 % (metals tabulated)
notes: value_si is the largest of the six. Polymers and elastomers are a different, large-strain machine.

observed_text: Elastic response follows the acoustic clock. Plastic flow is rate-dependent: Johnson–Cook factor 1 + C ln(strain rate in s⁻¹) with C from 0.006 (Nickel 200) to 0.060 (Armco iron), which is 1.08 to 1.83 at 10⁶ s⁻¹.
implied_text: The Hookean clock is the acoustic / Debye table. Plastic latency belongs to defect motion, not to the harmonic spring.
description: Microscopic restoration is acoustic-fast; yield latency is a different, slower defect clock.
value_text: acoustic restore; yield × (1.08–1.83) at 10⁶ s⁻¹
notes: Extrapolated from fits made up to about 10³ s⁻¹. Cold-spray strain rates are 10⁶–10⁹ s⁻¹.

observed_text: Small-strain elasticity is a restoring well, not a latch: stored energy ½ C ε² is returned on unload. Yield is a threshold on that well’s useful range. In crystals the microscopic barrier being crossed is a dislocation Peierls / pinning barrier — measured as a yield stress, not yet specified here as a KV-style node number.
implied_text: The Hookean machine stores and returns ½ C ε². It is not a directional memory. Yield is the well’s useful-range cliff, not a latch write.
description: Elastic energy is returned on unload. Yield is a range threshold, not a remanence barrier.
value_text: ½ C ε² returned; yield ≠ KV

observed_text: Yield constants at room temperature and 1 s⁻¹: OFHC copper 90 MPa, Nickel 200 163, Armco iron 175, 1006 steel 350, 2024-T351 aluminium 265, 4340 steel 792 MPa. Computed ideal shear strength: Al 1.85 GPa, Cu 2.65 GPa, which is 51–59 times the shear yield of OFHC copper and 12–14 times that of 2024 aluminium.
implied_text: Load above yield ends the linear output. Real yield is a mesoscale quantity, 12–59 times below the ideal shear strength in the cases worked.
description: Plastic set or fracture is the load-bearing failure of the Hookean machine. Real metallic yield is far below the ideal bond-breaking estimate.
value_text: yield 90–792 MPa; ideal shear strength 1.85–2.65 GPa
notes: value_si is OFHC copper. Yield is a convention on a continuous curve; it grows as d^(−1/2) with grain refinement and logarithmically with rate. The unsourced E/10 estimate was replaced.

observed_text: The crystal has a finite average shear modulus at its melting point; the liquid has none at acoustic frequencies. The loss of G at T_m is a jump. The liquid keeps a bulk modulus.
implied_text: The solid elastic machine dies with the grid. Compression can remain as a fluid K.
description: Melting removes the static shear modulus discontinuously. K survives.
value_text: G: finite → 0 at T_m (jump); fluid: no static shear
notes: Cross-cite melting and speed-of-sound. The first version read as a continuous softening.

observed_text: Young's modulus at 20 °C: Al 70.3, Ti 115.7, Cu 129.8, Ni 199.5–219.2, Fe 211.4, mild steel 211.9 GPa. Shear modulus: 26.1, 43.8, 48.3, 76.0–83.9, 81.6, 82.2 GPa. Bulk modulus of diamond 542 GPa.
implied_text: Handbook moduli {E, G, K} are the synchronized small-amplitude restoring output of the coupled nodes, together with a material- and history-dependent yield / fracture envelope.
description: The ion grid emits a GPa-class stiffness set. The same C is the slope v = √(C/ρ).
notes: value_si is mild steel. Speeds computed from K, G and density match measured sound speeds within 0.3 %.

observed_text: The computed ideal shear strength (5–9 % of the shear modulus) is 12–59 times the shear yield of the metals worked. That gap is the mesoscale dislocation and grain-boundary step, the mechanical counterpart of coercivity against anisotropy field.
implied_text: QSA does not yet have a clean buffer / barrier specification for dislocation nucleation and pinning. The Hookean output does not depend on closing it.
description: Yield / fracture is identified as a mesoscale envelope and is not reduced to a node-level barrier. Same unfinished step as magnet coercivity.
value_text: real yield 12–59× below ideal shear strength; mesoscale
notes: Cross-cite ferromagnetic-hysteresis and permanent-magnet-latch (Hc ≪ Ha). File-level mapping is Medium.

observed_text: Of the 32 crystal classes 21 have no centre of symmetry and 20 of those are piezoelectric (class 432 is the exception). A centrosymmetric crystal of any size has no linear coupling. A ceramic needs a net poled direction.
implied_text: The hardware is an inversion-free grid. Size does not create d_ij if inversion is present. Polar memory of a poled ferroelectric is owned by ferroelectric-remanence.
description: The linear strain–polarization machine is provisioned only by a non-centrosymmetric lattice (20 of 32 classes).
value_text: 20 of 32 classes piezoelectric (21 non-centrosymmetric)
notes: Corrected: the first version said 20 classes lack inversion. Electrostriction is quadratic and is not this entry.

observed_text: The mechanical side follows the acoustic clocks of elasticity and speed-of-sound; the electrical side follows the dielectric response. No clock number is filed in this entry.
implied_text: Device latency is the acoustic transit / plate resonance, not an atomic piezo clock.
description: No single atomic piezo period is extracted. Laboratory clocks sit at the plate resonance.
value_text: plate resonance / acoustic transit (unpinned)
notes: Cross-cite speed-of-sound and refraction-dielectric. No source opened for a device resonance.

observed_text: The existence condition is the crystal class, not an energy barrier. Quartz needs no poling. A ferroelectric ceramic is poled slightly below its Curie point and loses the poled state above it.
implied_text: Linear piezo is a symmetry-gated coupling, not a memory. Ferroelectric remnant P is a different machine sharing some crystals.
description: No piezo latch. The gate is inversion-free symmetry; quartz does not die with a remnant-P write.
value_text: inversion-free gate; not a KV / P_r latch
notes: Cross-cite ferroelectric-remanence, which owns the poled state.

observed_text: With a centre of symmetry, or in class 432, every linear coefficient is zero.
implied_text: If inversion is a symmetry, the linear output is forbidden, independent of field strength short of breakdown.
description: Inversion present → d_ij = 0. As sharp a hardware condition as the plasma-frequency clock on reflection.
value_text: centre of symmetry (or class 432) ⇒ d_ijk = 0
notes: Exact by symmetry.

observed_text: Above the Curie point each crystallite of a perovskite ceramic is cubic with no dipole moment: BaTiO3 120 °C (393 K), PZT5H 195 °C, PZT4 320 °C, PZT5A 365 °C. A ceramic can depole below it (187 °C against a Curie point of 325 °C in Na0.5Bi0.5TiO3). Quartz has a structural inversion at 573.3 °C.
implied_text: PZT fails as a large piezo at ferroelectric T_C even while a solid remains. Quartz fails only by losing the non-centrosymmetric grid.
description: Ferroelectric piezo has a T_C collapse of the large d_ij. Quartz does not share that cliff.
value_text: T > Tc: 393 K (BaTiO3); 468–638 K (PZT grades)
notes: value_si is BaTiO3. Depoling below Tc is a separate, gradual route (crossover). Whether β-quartz stays piezoelectric was not settled by an opened source.

observed_text: Melting or breakdown removes the lattice or the insulator. Short of that, a substrate clamps a film (AlN 1.8 pm/V clamped against 5.6 pm/V in the free crystal) and quartz d11 falls 11 % between −196 °C and 100 °C.
implied_text: No inversion-free solid, no linear d_ij. Shock-depoling or cracking is lattice damage, not a second copy of melting.
description: Melting or cracking destroys the strain–polarization hardware with the lattice.
value_text: melting / breakdown; clamping and temperature drift
notes: Cross-cite melting and dielectric-breakdown. The clamping and drift parts are continuous.

observed_text: Quartz d11 = 2.25–2.31 pm/V. AlN d33 = 5.6 pm/V (single crystal), 3.4–5.15 (polycrystalline). BaTiO3 d33 = 85.6 (crystal), 190 pC/N (ceramic). PZT d33 = 225–618 pC/N across PZT8, PZT4, PZT5A, PZT5H. PVDF d33 = −21 to −27 pC/N.
implied_text: A linear, reversible strain ↔ polarization conversion with a material-typical d_ij, present only while the inversion-free (and, if ferroelectric, polar) lattice holds.
description: The coupling output is a pC/N-class d_ij: quartz ~2, PZT ~10², only inside the symmetry / polar envelope.
value_text: quartz 2.3; AlN 3.4–5.6; BaTiO3 86–190; PZT 225–618; PVDF −21 to −27 pC/N
notes: value_si is quartz d11. BaTiO3 crystal, LiNbO3 and PVDF values are from a tertiary list; the BaTiO3 ceramic value is a search excerpt.

observed_text: The mapping takes measured d_ijk. The factor of 270 between quartz d11 and PZT5H d33 is not derived, and in ceramics part of the coefficient is domain-wall motion.
implied_text: The symmetry gate and T_C collapse are located; the magnitude of d is taken, not computed.
description: Coupling magnitude is a handbook input. That is the principal reason the mapping is medium rather than high.
value_text: d_ijk taken (quartz 2.3 vs PZT5H 618 pC/N)
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Polar latch is a different machine sharing the same crystal.

observed_text: An ordered magnetic population in a deformable lattice. A body free to deform takes up the strain with no stress; when the deformation is hindered a stress λ_s E/(1+ν) appears instead: 5.3 MPa in nickel, or Eλ_s = 7.0–8.8 MPa for a bar held at both ends.
implied_text: Hardware is ordered M plus a strain-carrying grid. Grain-scale latching of M is owned by permanent-magnet-latch / superparamagnetism; this file owns the strain that follows M.
description: Magnetostriction needs an ordered moment and a deformable lattice. Stress appears only under constraint and is 5–9 MPa in nickel.
value_text: ordered M + deformable lattice; clamped stress 5–9 MPa (Ni)
notes: Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch. A free particle changes shape without stress.

observed_text: No clock of its own. Magnetic side: the domain-wall and rotation clocks of the magnet entries. Mechanical side: the acoustic transit of elasticity.
implied_text: The length-change clock is the magnet’s write / wall motion plus acoustic transit, not the Larmor carrier.
description: No separate magnetostrictive period is extracted. Lab loops are sweep- and wall-limited.
value_text: magnet clocks + acoustic transit; none of its own
notes: No source opened on dynamic or cyclic magnetostriction.

observed_text: No separate magnetostrictive latch. The thresholds are the host magnet's: the Curie point (nickel 631 K) and the field that aligns the moment (nickel [100]: 300 Oe internal). The elastic energy of a clamped 35 ppm strain in nickel is 122 J m⁻³, equal to a temperature rise of 3.1×10⁻⁵ K.
implied_text: This file must not re-specify the magnet. Strain is locked to M; the barrier that holds M is the latch’s.
description: Magnetostriction is a coupling, not a latch. T_C, KV, and coercivity stay with permanent-magnet-latch.
value_text: T_C 631 K (Ni); 300 Oe internal; ½Eλ² = 122 J/m³
notes: Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch. The inverse (Villari) effect is measured: stress changes the magnetization.

observed_text: The saturation strain falls to zero at the Curie point: nickel 631 K (358–360 °C), iron 1042 K. Below it the strain falls continuously with the magnetization, most steeply close to the transition; nickel λ100 is −57 to −60 ppm near 0 K and −46 ppm at room temperature.
implied_text: T > T_C → ordered moment gone → λ = 0. This file owns the length change, not the latch.
description: Magnetostriction dies at the host Curie point with the ordered moment.
value_text: T > T_C (Ni 631 K; Fe 1042 K)
notes: value_si is the nickel Curie point. Terfenol-D Curie temperature not found; Galfenol 700 °C.

observed_text: Melting removes the solid. No opened source supports shock scrambling a magnet through this coupling. The full saturation strain of nickel, clamped, gives 7.0–8.8 MPa, which is 4.3–5.4 % of the 163 MPa yield constant of Nickel 200; the elastic strain at yield is 23 times the magnetostrictive strain.
implied_text: No lattice, no strain. Magnetostrictive stress in nickel is about a twentieth of yield, so this coupling does not by itself produce plastic damage.
description: Lattice loss is melting. Static magnetostrictive stress in nickel is far below yield.
value_text: melting; clamped stress 4–5 % of yield (Ni)
notes: Corrected: the first version treated shock through this coupling as a mechanical failure path. Cyclic loading not sourced.

observed_text: The strain follows M(H) and saturates. Nickel [100] saturates at an internal field of 300 Oe; a 5:1 ellipsoid needed 650 Oe applied, and an isolated sphere needs about 0.23 T. Composition can remove the coupling: 7 at.% Ga takes nickel from −35 to −10 ppm.
implied_text: Macroscopic ΔL is small if M is not aligned, even when λ_s is finite. Alignment is a domain / coercivity condition, not a second coupling.
description: Below saturation the macroscopic strain is partial. The applied field needed depends on shape through the demagnetizing factor.
value_text: 300 Oe internal (Ni); ~0.23 T applied for a sphere
notes: Cross-cite magnetic-domains and ferromagnetic-hysteresis. The strain is even in M: reversal leaves it unchanged.

observed_text: Room temperature: nickel −35 to −40 ppm polycrystalline (λ100 −46, λ111 −24); iron −9 ppm (λ100 20, λ111 −21); Galfenol about 400 ppm; Terfenol-D 1000–2000 ppm depending on field and prestress (λ100 90, λ111 1640).
implied_text: A saturation strain λ_s locked to the aligned moment, plus the inverse stress–M channel, while the ordered magnet and the lattice both remain.
description: The strain output is a material number from −9 ppm (Fe) and −40 ppm (Ni) to 400 ppm (Galfenol) and above 1000 ppm (Terfenol-D), fixed to the axis of the moment.
value_text: Ni −33 to −40 ppm; Fe −9; Galfenol 400; Terfenol-D 1000–2000 ppm
notes: Joule strain conserves volume; volume magnetostriction is separate. The whole strain of nickel equals the thermal expansion from a 2.6–3.0 K rise.

observed_text: Why λ_s is 4×10⁻⁵ in nickel and 10⁻³ in Terfenol-D is taken as data, the same way d_33 is taken as data on piezoelectricity.
implied_text: The T_C and lattice-destruction collapses are located; λ_s is a handbook coupling.
description: Coupling magnitude is taken, not derived from a stated node-level spring. Mapping confidence is therefore medium.
value_text: λ_s taken (4×10⁻⁵ Ni; 10⁻³ Terfenol-D)
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch: do not re-specify remanence, T_C, or KV here.

observed_text: A mechanically coupled lattice whose wells are not purely quadratic, large enough for a macroscopic length to be defined. If the restoring wells are purely quadratic, ⟨x⟩ is independent of T and α = 0. The harmonic grid that already produces speed-of-sound, elasticity, and debye-cutoff is not sufficient.
implied_text: Expansion is the anharmonic correction to the same ion-grid hardware. Harmonic springs provision moduli and a long-wave slope and still give α = 0.
description: The extra hardware is anharmonicity (γ ≠ 0), not a fourth reading of the harmonic springs.
value_text: γ ≠ 0 anharmonic wells; harmonic grid insufficient
notes: Invar adds a magnetic volume term. The harmonic-lattice statement is textbook and was not sourced. Anharmonicity does not fix the sign: Si and fused silica contract on heating at 100 K.

observed_text: There is no separate expansion clock. The lattice clocks are the phonon spectrum; α(T) is the thermal occupation of those modes acting through γ. The laboratory length change follows the thermal equilibration time of the specimen, not an atomic period.
implied_text: α is an occupation readout of the existing phonon table, delayed only by specimen thermalization.
description: No dedicated expansion period is extracted. Laboratory ΔL follows thermal equilibration.
value_text: no separate clock; follows thermal equilibration
notes: Cross-cite phonon-dispersion and thermal-equilibrium-temperature.

observed_text: No latched barrier and no threshold number. The operating condition is anharmonic wells plus a finite temperature. There is no measured threshold at which expansion appears. No table of Grüneisen parameters was opened.
implied_text: Expansion is not a gated latch.
description: No activation barrier and no γ_c. Anharmonic wells plus finite T are the operating condition.
value_text: no threshold; γ not sourced
notes: γ → 0 is the harmonic-limit statement.

observed_text: A purely harmonic lattice would not expand: its mean spacing is independent of amplitude. This is a limiting condition on the wells and no material reaches it. Negative expansion exists (silicon −0.4, fused silica −0.53 ×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹ at 100 K), so anharmonicity does not fix the sign.
implied_text: Remove anharmonicity and the length-change machine disappears, even though moduli, sound speed, and the 3N mode count remain.
description: The harmonic lattice does not expand. That is the named collapse of this effect.
value_text: γ → 0 ⇒ α = 0 (harmonic limit)
notes: Harmonic statement is textbook, not sourced; the negative values are measured.

observed_text: α falls toward zero at low temperature: copper 16.5 at 293 K and 10.3 at 100 K; diamond 1.0 and 0.05 (10⁻⁶ K⁻¹). It keeps rising with temperature up to melting: aluminium 12.2 at 100 K and 34.0 at 800 K.
implied_text: Starve C_V and expansion stops even if γ is finite. Melting ends the solid’s α spec; it is not an α cliff.
description: Low T kills α with the heat capacity. Melting ends the solid; α itself has no T_C-style pin.
value_text: α → 0 as T → 0 (Cu 16.5 → 10.3 at 100 K); rises to T_m
notes: Cross-cite debye-cutoff (C_V) and melting (high-T end of the same wells).

observed_text: Invar (64 Fe, 36 Ni): 1.4 at 100 K, 0.53 at 200 K, 0.13 at 293 K, 5.1 at 500 K and 17.1 at 800 K (10⁻⁶ K⁻¹); iron is 11.8 at 293 K. The low value is confined to a window near room temperature. The magnetic-volume explanation is cited and was not opened.
implied_text: α ≈ 0 without harmonic wells. That is not the harmonic-limit collapse.
description: Invar's near-zero α is a compensation confined to a temperature window, not harmonic wells.
value_text: Invar 0.13×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹ at 293 K; 5.1 at 500 K
notes: Cross-cite magnetostriction (volume channel). Iron expands 91 times as much at 293 K.

observed_text: Linear expansivity at 293 K, in 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹: W 4.5, Ti 8.6, Fe 11.8, Ni 13.4, Cu 16.5, Al 23.1, Zn 30.2.
implied_text: A small, material-typical α(T) as the averaged length change of an anharmonic, thermally occupied grid.
description: The expansion machine emits a material-typical α(T): 4.5–30 ×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹ for the metals tabulated at 293 K.
value_text: 4.5–30 ×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹ at 293 K (W to Zn)
notes: value_si left null: class, not one pin. Corrected from 10⁻⁶–10⁻⁵.

observed_text: Anharmonicity is the stated condition and not a single hardware number. There is no measured threshold at which expansion turns on. QSA does not derive the 4.5–30 ×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹ class from node-well shapes.
implied_text: The resource (anharmonicity) is named; its strength is taken as data. Invar shows that α ≈ 0 can also be a cancellation, which must not be misread as γ = 0.
description: Expansion is located as the anharmonic correction, but that resource is not pinned to one measured hardware number the way ω_p or T_m is.
value_text: α class taken; no threshold
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Quasi-harmonic ω(q) shifts organize data and do not supply a single how-anharmonic number.

observed_text: Recoilless emission and absorption occur in the solid state, crystalline or non-crystalline, and not for free atoms, gases or liquids. Free 57Fe has E_R = 1.96 meV against Γ = 4.64 neV (ratio 4.2e5).
implied_text: The host that binds the nucleus is the buffer; crystalline order is not required. A free atom is under-provisioned.
description: Recoilless resonance needs a binding host in which the nucleus neither recoils freely nor diffuses during the nuclear lifetime.
value_text: binding solid host (crystalline or not); not a free atom
notes: Bragg order is not the resource: non-crystalline solids support the effect.

observed_text: 57Fe 14.4 keV state: half-life 98.3(3) ns, mean life 141.8 ns, which sets Γ = 4.64 neV. The host vibration spectrum sets f.
implied_text: Nuclear lifetime plus host phonon clock.
description: Γ from nuclear τ; f from the grid clock.

observed_text: 57Fe line at 14.4129(6) keV with natural width Γ = 4.64 neV. One natural width corresponds to a Doppler velocity of 0.097 mm/s.
implied_text: Nuclear line plus lattice recoilless condition. Not an under-threshold 14.4 keV gate.
description: Overlap within Γ is the operating window.

observed_text: f = exp(−k²⟨x²⟩) falls continuously with temperature. In tin the absorption drops rapidly and the line broadens in the last few degrees below melting, assigned to self-diffusion (about 1e-8 cm²/s at 0.6 K below T_m). The effect is not achieved in ordinary liquids. Model diffusive width 2ħk²D: equal to Γ at D = 6.6e-16 m²/s for 57Fe, about 9e5 Γ at D = 0.6e-9 m²/s.
implied_text: The resonance is lost through rising ⟨x²⟩ and through diffusion, both continuous; the loss near melting begins in the solid.
description: No recoilless, narrow line once the nucleus recoils freely or diffuses within the nuclear lifetime.
value_text: f falls with T; diffusion width 2ħk²D; no resonance in gas or ordinary liquid
notes: Not a threshold at T_m. No numeric f(T) for a named host was opened.

observed_text: Recoilless resonant absorption in a solid host, scanned with Doppler velocities on the scale cΓ/Eγ = 0.097 mm/s for 57Fe.
implied_text: The lattice-enabled nuclear line is the output.
description: Recoilless resonance as the stable output.
value_text: recoilless absorption

observed_text: 14.4 keV is the line energy, not an under-threshold non-occurrence of this channel.
implied_text: Do not file as an energy-gate whose collapse is Eγ<14.4 keV.
description: Lattice-mode payload, not a 14.4 keV under-threshold gate.
value_text: Eγ is the line, not a threshold
